react-perf-0-0-0.summary: This course focuses on measuring React app performance precisely and fixing slowdowns one change at a time using techniques like memo, useMemo, and useCallback.
questions: What is the main approach to improving React app performance in this course?
Why is it important to measure performance before and after changes?
Which React hooks are commonly associated with performance optimization?

react-perf-0-0-1.summary: The app to be optimized is a trading dashboard with 5000 live-updating rows, filtering, and sorting, designed to challenge React's rendering performance.
questions: What kind of app is used to demonstrate React performance issues?
Why is the trading dashboard app challenging for React?
What features does the dashboard include that affect performance?

react-perf-0-0-2.summary: The project structure includes components and a custom hook useTicks.js that simulates live price updates, with Dashboard.jsx managing state inefficiently to demonstrate performance issues.
questions: What files and components make up the project structure?
What does the useTicks.js custom hook do?
How is state managed in Dashboard.jsx and why is it inefficient?

react-perf-0-0-3.summary: Typing in the filter input causes visible lag due to inefficient rendering, illustrating a common performance bug where UI is slow but functionally correct.
questions: What happens when typing in the filter box in the initial app?
Why is the UI slow even though it works correctly?
What are possible causes of the lag when filtering?

react-perf-0-0-4.summary: The course roadmap covers React rendering fundamentals, profiling with React DevTools, state placement, memoization, React.memo, useCallback, virtualization, and final performance comparisons.
questions: What topics are covered in the React Performance Patterns course?
Which chapter focuses on profiling React apps?
What techniques are taught to reduce rendering and improve performance?

react-perf-0-1-0.summary: React rendering involves two distinct phases: the render phase and the commit phase, which clarifies common performance misconceptions.
questions: What are the two phases of React rendering?
Why is it important to distinguish render phase from commit phase in React?
How do render and commit phases relate to React performance?

react-perf-0-1-1.summary: The render phase in React calls the component function to produce React elements describing the UI without touching the DOM, making rendering a pure computation.
questions: What happens during the React render phase?
Why is React rendering considered a pure function?
Does React update the DOM during the render phase?

react-perf-0-1-2.summary: The commit phase compares new and previous React element trees (reconciliation) and updates the DOM only if differences exist, avoiding unnecessary browser work.
questions: What is reconciliation in React?
When does React update the DOM?
Can a component render without causing DOM changes?

react-perf-0-1-3.summary: Logging renders and enabling paint flashing reveals many React renders but few DOM commits, highlighting wasted JavaScript work to optimize.
questions: How can you observe React renders versus DOM commits?
Why do many React renders not cause DOM updates?
What does paint flashing show in React performance debugging?

react-perf-0-1-4.summary: Renders do not rebuild the DOM and are usually cheap; the goal is to avoid unnecessary renders that produce no UI changes, especially in large lists.
questions: Does every React render rebuild the DOM?
Why are some React renders considered expensive?
How can you reduce unnecessary React renders?

react-perf-0-2-0.summary: React re-renders components based on a short list of triggers, which will be explained and demonstrated using console logs in Dashboard.jsx.
questions: What triggers a React component to re-render?
How can I identify what causes re-renders in React?

react-perf-0-2-1.summary: React re-renders a component when its state changes, when context values change, or when its parent re-renders; props changes alone do not trigger re-renders by default.
questions: Does changing props trigger a React component to re-render?
What are the main triggers for React component re-renders?
How does React.memo affect re-rendering related to props?

react-perf-0-2-2.summary: Typing in a filter state triggers Dashboard to re-render, causing PriceTable and all PriceRow components to re-render even if their data hasn't changed, demonstrating React's default re-render behavior.
questions: What causes Dashboard and its child components to re-render?
Why do all PriceRow components re-render even if their data is unchanged?
How does React handle re-rendering when a parent component updates state?

react-perf-0-2-3.summary: Frequent state updates high in the component tree, like from a live feed, cause all descendants to re-render, so React relies on memoization and state placement to optimize performance.
questions: How do frequent state updates affect React rendering performance?
Why does React re-render all children when state changes high in the tree?
How can memoization help with React performance?

react-perf-0-2-4.summary: Changing refs or local variables does not trigger re-renders, and React usually bails out if a setter is called with the same value; the main triggers remain state, context, and parent renders.
questions: Does changing a ref cause a React component to re-render?
What happens if a state setter is called with the same value?
What are the confirmed triggers for React re-renders?

react-perf-0-3-0.summary: React uses shallow equality with Object.is to compare props and state, which is key to understanding when memoization works or fails silently.
questions: What comparison method does React use to check if props or state changed?
Why is understanding shallow equality important for React performance?

react-perf-0-3-1.summary: Object.is returns true for equal primitives but false for distinct objects with identical contents, since object equality is based on reference, not content.
questions: How does Object.is compare primitive values?
Why does Object.is return false for two objects with the same contents?
What does object equality mean in JavaScript?

react-perf-0-3-2.summary: React.memo performs a shallow comparison by running Object.is on each prop value one level deep, so new object references cause re-renders even if contents are unchanged.
questions: What does shallow comparison mean in React.memo?
Why does passing a new object literal as a prop cause re-renders?
How deep does React.memo compare props?

react-perf-0-3-3.summary: React compares props and state by reference, so creating new arrays or functions inline causes memoized components to re-render unnecessarily.
questions: Why does a memoized component re-render when receiving an array created inline?
How does React compare dependencies in useEffect and useMemo?
Why does creating a new function inline cause re-renders in React?

react-perf-0-3-4.summary: React uses cheap reference checks (not deep comparisons) to detect changes, so developers must keep references stable using useMemo for values and useCallback for functions.
questions: Why does React use reference checks instead of deep comparisons?
How can developers keep references stable to avoid unnecessary renders?
What React hooks help maintain stable references for values and functions?

react-perf-1-0-0.summary: Use the React DevTools Profiler in a development build to measure React component performance on your dashboard, noting that production builds run faster and absolute times are relative.
questions: How do I set up React DevTools Profiler for performance measurement?
Why should I profile a development build instead of production?
What tabs appear in React DevTools after installation?

react-perf-1-0-1.summary: Enable 'record why each component rendered' in Profiler settings, then record exactly one user interaction per session to get clear performance data.
questions: How do I configure React Profiler to see why components rendered?
Why should I record only one interaction per profiling session?
What is the recommended workflow for profiling user actions?

react-perf-1-0-2.summary: The Profiler's commit chart shows the time React takes to commit changes; a single keystroke causing a 90ms commit is too slow for smooth 60fps interaction, which needs under 16ms.
questions: What does each bar in the React Profiler commit chart represent?
Why is 90 milliseconds per keystroke considered slow?
What is the target commit time for smooth UI interactions?

react-perf-1-0-3.summary: Use the flame graph to identify which components rendered and why, confirming if child components re-render due to parent renders without prop changes.
questions: How can I tell why a component rendered in React Profiler?
What does a gray component mean in the flame graph?
How do parent renders affect child component rendering?

react-perf-1-0-4.summary: The ranked view in React Profiler sorts components by render time, revealing many small but costly renders (like thousands of PriceRow components) causing performance issues.
questions: How does the ranked view help identify slow components?
What does seeing many small slow components indicate?
What is the next step after identifying expensive components in profiling?

react-perf-1-1-0.summary: Learn to read React Profiler flame graphs to identify wasted renders, which are component renders producing unchanged output, using a live price tick example.
questions: What is a wasted render in React?
How can the React Profiler help identify wasted renders?
What does a flame graph show in React performance profiling?

react-perf-1-1-1.summary: The flame graph shows that some components like FilterBar re-render without prop changes, but small wasted renders may not need fixing; focus on costly renders using the ranked view.
questions: How can I identify wasted renders in a React flame graph?
Why might a component re-render even if its props haven't changed?
When should I ignore small wasted renders in performance analysis?

react-perf-1-1-2.summary: A pattern of many sibling components rendering with unchanged props, blamed on the parent, indicates a major wasted render cost that memoization can fix.
questions: What pattern indicates a large wasted render cost in React?
How can memoization help with many sibling components rendering unnecessarily?
What does the 'parent rendered, props unchanged' tooltip mean?

react-perf-1-1-3.summary: Use the commit chart to find components rendering too often, distinguishing between many small renders (memoize children) and few expensive renders (avoid recomputing) for optimization.
questions: How do I use the commit chart to detect excessive component renders?
What does a fat bar versus many thin bars in the ranked view indicate?
When should I memoize children versus avoid recomputing in React?

react-perf-1-1-4.summary: Identify key performance issues: high state in Dashboard causing re-renders, expensive filter/sort computations, unnecessary PriceRow renders, and inline props defeating memoization.
questions: What are common causes of wasted renders in this dashboard example?
How does state location affect component re-renders?
Why can inline functions and objects defeat memoization?

react-perf-2-0-0.summary: Place state in the component where it is used to minimize re-renders of large subtrees, since parent re-renders cause all children to re-render.
questions: Why should state be placed where it is used in React?
What happens to child components when a parent component re-renders?
How does moving state down affect React component re-renders?

react-perf-2-0-1.summary: State used by multiple components, like filter text, must stay higher, but state used by only one small component, like hoveredSymbol, can be moved down to reduce unnecessary re-renders.
questions: When should state be kept high in the component tree?
Which state is a good candidate to move down in React?
How does shared state affect component re-renders?

react-perf-2-0-2.summary: Moving hoveredSymbol state and its handlers into a new SymbolTooltip component reduces re-renders drastically, improving hover performance by 30x without memoization.
questions: How can moving state into a smaller component improve performance?
What was the performance improvement after moving hoveredSymbol state?
Why did moving hoveredSymbol state reduce re-renders?

react-perf-2-0-3.summary: Lifting content up means rendering expensive children in the parent and passing them as children props to a stateful wrapper, preventing unnecessary re-renders when the wrapper's state changes.
questions: What does lifting content up mean in React?
How does passing children as props prevent re-renders?
Why lift content up when a stateful wrapper surrounds expensive children?

react-perf-2-0-4.summary: Because children props keep the same reference when created by the parent, React skips re-rendering them when the wrapper's state changes; move state down or lift content up before using memoization.
questions: Why does React skip re-rendering children with the same reference?
What is the recommended order of optimization techniques before memoization?
How does reference equality affect React rendering?

react-perf-2-1-0.summary: Filtering and sorting a large list on every render causes performance issues in Dashboard.jsx, as these computations run on every price tick, keystroke, and selection change.
questions: Why does filtering and sorting on every render cause performance problems?
What operations are causing heavy computation in Dashboard.jsx?
When does the filtering and sorting run in the Dashboard component?

react-perf-2-1-1.summary: Using console.time reveals filtering and sorting take about 11ms per render, even when inputs haven't changed, highlighting the need for memoization to avoid redundant computations.
questions: How can you measure the time taken by filtering and sorting in React?
Why is memoization needed for filtering and sorting in this case?
What does console.time show about the cost of filtering and sorting?

react-perf-2-1-2.summary: Memoization caches expensive computation results and React's useMemo hook recomputes only when specified dependencies change, optimizing computed state.
questions: What is memoization and how does it improve performance?
How does useMemo determine when to recompute a value?
What dependencies should be included when memoizing visibleRows?

react-perf-2-1-3.summary: useMemo memoizes the filtered and sorted rows by running the computation only when dependencies (rows, filter, sortKey) change, preventing unnecessary recalculations on re-renders.
questions: How does useMemo help optimize filtering and sorting in React?
What dependencies should be included in useMemo for filtering and sorting?
How does React decide whether to recompute useMemo's function?

react-perf-2-1-4.summary: useMemo memoizes computed values, while useCallback memoizes function references; useCallback is needed to prevent child re-renders when passing callbacks to memoized children.
questions: What is the difference between useMemo and useCallback?
When should you use useCallback in React?
How do useCallback and React.memo work together to prevent unnecessary child renders?

react-perf-2-1-5.summary: Memoization with useMemo avoids redundant filtering and sorting unless inputs change, but overusing it can add overhead; new arrays cause recomputation, which is expected behavior.
questions: What is the main benefit of memoization for computed state?
Why can overusing useMemo hurt performance?
Why does useMemo recompute when a new rows array arrives?

react-perf-2-2-0.summary: useMemo has a performance cost due to storing values and comparing dependencies, so avoid wrapping everything in it without measuring its benefit.
questions: What is the performance cost of using useMemo in React?
Why shouldn't you wrap every calculation in useMemo?
How does React handle dependencies in useMemo?

react-perf-2-2-1.summary: Memoizing a calculation with changing dependencies every render can cause extra overhead, making useMemo slower than just recalculating.
questions: What happens if useMemo dependencies change every render?
How does useMemo behave when the dependency array contains a new array each tick?
Why can useMemo cause slower performance in some cases?

react-perf-2-2-2.summary: Memoizing trivial computations like string concatenation or small additions wastes time because dependency checks cost more; measure with console.time and memoize only if calculation takes about a millisecond or more.
questions: When is memoizing trivial computations counterproductive?
How can you measure if a calculation is worth memoizing?
What rule of thumb does React documentation suggest for using useMemo?

react-perf-2-2-3.summary: Incorrect or missing dependencies in useMemo cause stale outputs; enable the ESLint rule react-hooks/exhaustive-deps to catch these bugs and avoid silencing it.
questions: What happens if useMemo dependencies are incomplete?
How can you detect missing dependencies in useMemo?
Why is a memoization bug worse than a performance issue?

react-perf-2-2-4.summary: Decide to use useMemo only if restructuring state doesn't help and the computation is slow with stable inputs; otherwise, avoid it to prevent wasted work.
questions: What is the decision process for using useMemo effectively?
When should you remove useMemo from a calculation?
What tools help avoid unnecessary re-renders besides useMemo?

react-perf-3-0-0.summary: React.memo prevents unnecessary re-renders of PriceRow components by skipping updates when props remain unchanged.
questions: What does React.memo do for a component?
How can React.memo help with many PriceRow components re-rendering?
What props does the PriceRow component receive?

react-perf-3-0-1.summary: React.memo skips re-renders if props are shallowly equal, but new object or function references cause re-renders, shown by wrapping PriceRow with React.memo.
questions: When does React.memo skip re-rendering a component?
Why do new function or object references cause React.memo to re-render?
How do you apply React.memo to a component?

react-perf-3-0-2.summary: Passing a new inline arrow function as a prop causes React.memo to fail because each render creates a new function reference, triggering re-renders despite memoization.
questions: Why does passing an inline arrow function as a prop cause re-renders with React.memo?
What is the reference trap in React.memo?
How does creating a new function on every render affect memoized components?

react-perf-3-0-3.summary: useCallback stabilizes function references across renders, enabling React.memo to skip re-renders when passing callbacks as props, demonstrated by memoizing handleSelect.
questions: How does useCallback help React.memo optimize re-renders?
What does the dependency array in useCallback control?
Why is useCallback used for the onSelect callback in Dashboard?

react-perf-3-0-4.summary: Using React.memo with PriceRow reduces re-renders from five thousand to a few hundred, improving performance significantly, especially when combined with useCallback.
questions: How does React.memo affect the flame graph and commit time?
Why do React.memo and useCallback need to be used together?
What happens when typing in the filter after applying React.memo?

react-perf-3-1-0.summary: React.memo optimizations can silently fail if inline objects, arrays, or functions are passed as props, so avoiding inline definitions helps maintain memo's effectiveness.
questions: Why does React.memo optimization sometimes silently fail?
What common prop patterns break React.memo?
How can inline objects or functions affect memoization?

react-perf-3-1-1.summary: Passing inline style objects like style={{ color: ... }} creates new object references each render, causing React.memo to re-render components unnecessarily.
questions: Why does passing style={{ color: ... }} break React.memo?
How does React.memo detect prop changes with objects?
How can Profiler help identify memo re-renders?

react-perf-3-1-2.summary: To avoid breaking memo, pass primitives instead of objects, hoist constant objects outside components, or use useMemo to memoize objects dependent on props or state.
questions: How can passing primitives improve React.memo performance?
What does hoisting constants outside components achieve?
When should useMemo be used for object props?

react-perf-3-1-3.summary: To avoid creating new closures each render, pass a stable function prop and the data separately, letting the child component combine them to keep props stable and memo effective.
questions: How can inline arrow functions in props cause performance issues?
What is a pattern to avoid per-render closures in React props?
How do you pass callbacks and data separately to maintain stable props?

react-perf-3-1-4.summary: Passing JSX as children creates new element objects each render, causing memoized components to re-render; use Profiler and React DevTools to identify and debug these cases.
questions: Why does passing JSX as children break React.memo?
How can Profiler and React DevTools help debug memo re-renders?
What does the Memo badge in React DevTools indicate?

react-perf-3-2-0.summary: Context can cause re-render storms in React because components using useContext re-render on any context value change, bypassing React.memo optimizations.
questions: Why does using context cause re-render storms in React?
How does useContext affect component re-rendering?
What is the downside of passing many values through a single context?

react-perf-3-2-1.summary: Using useContext causes all consuming components to re-render when the context value changes, bypassing React.memo optimizations that only prevent parent-triggered re-renders.
questions: What happens to components using useContext when the context value changes?
Does React.memo prevent re-renders caused by context updates?
Why do all rows re-render when the context provider value changes?

react-perf-3-2-2.summary: Context provider value objects created inline cause new references on every render, triggering re-renders in all consumers even if only unrelated fields change.
questions: Why does creating the context value inline cause re-renders?
What happens when any field in the context value changes?
Can context consumers select only part of the context value?

react-perf-3-2-3.summary: Splitting context into smaller focused contexts and memoizing provider values with useMemo reduces unnecessary re-renders by limiting updates to relevant consumers.
questions: How can splitting context reduce re-render storms?
Why use useMemo on context provider values?
Which contexts should components subscribe to for optimal rendering?

react-perf-3-2-4.summary: Separating state setters into their own stable dispatch contexts prevents components that only trigger updates from re-rendering when state changes, further optimizing performance.
questions: How does separating setters into their own context help performance?
What is a dispatch context in React?
Why do components that only call setters not re-render on state changes?

react-perf-4-0-0.summary: Virtualization (windowing) improves performance by rendering only visible rows plus a buffer instead of all 5,000 rows in the DOM.
questions: What is virtualization or windowing in rendering large lists?
Why does rendering all 5,000 rows cause performance issues?

react-perf-4-0-1.summary: Virtualization uses a fixed-height container with overflow auto and a tall empty div to simulate full scroll height, rendering only visible rows absolutely positioned.

What CSS properties are used to implement virtualization in a table?
How are visible rows positioned in a virtualized list?

questions: How do you calculate which rows are visible in a virtualized list?
What is overscan and why is it used in virtualization?

react-perf-4-0-3.summary: Production virtualization is best done with libraries like react-window or TanStack Virtual that handle edge cases and provide cached style objects to maintain memoization.
questions: What are recommended libraries for virtualization in React?
How do virtualization libraries help with variable row heights and accessibility?
Why do virtualization libraries provide cached style objects?

react-perf-4-0-4.summary: Virtualization reduces DOM nodes from 5,000 to about 30, cutting render time from 300ms to under 10ms, but has accessibility trade-offs requiring aria attributes.
questions: How much does virtualization reduce render time and DOM nodes?
